body.objective: Students will be able to feel compound metre.
successCriteria: I can tell simple metre from compound metre
I can count and perform rhythms in 6/8
I can recognize compound metre in music
body.hook: Clap along to a jig, a lullaby or many Celtic and folk tunes, and you'll notice the beat seems to bounce in threes: ONE-two-three, FOUR-five-six. That bouncing feel comes from compound metre, and it's a different way of organizing time from most pop songs.

vocabulary.definition: The way beats are grouped in music.
A metre where each beat divides into two, such as 2/4, 3/4 and 4/4.
A metre where each beat divides into three, such as 6/8.
A compound metre with six eighth notes per bar, felt as two main beats.
In 6/8, the note that lasts one main beat (three eighth notes).

study.title: Twos and Threes
study.question: How is compound metre different from simple metre?
study.passage:
Simple vs compound:
• Simple metre (2/4, 3/4, 4/4): each beat splits into two eighth notes: "1-and 2-and."
• Compound metre (6/8): each beat splits into three eighth notes: "1-la-li 2-la-li."
In 6/8 there are six eighth notes per bar, but you feel two main beats, on eighth notes 1 and 4. A dotted quarter note lasts one main beat.
Part 1, Feel it (5 minutes): Count "1-2-3-4-5-6" with accents on 1 and 4 while stepping on the accents.
Part 2, Compare (10 minutes): The teacher plays two short clips: one in 4/4 (a march or pop song) and one in 6/8 (a jig or a lullaby). Students step to each and describe the difference. Public-domain examples in 6/8 include "Pop Goes the Weasel" and "Row, Row, Row Your Boat."
Part 3, Read (10 minutes), in 6/8:
Line 1: dotted quarter, dotted quarter
Line 2: three eighth notes, dotted quarter
Line 3: quarter, eighth, quarter, eighth
Line 4: six eighth notes
Part 4, Create (10 minutes): In pairs, write a two-bar rhythm in 6/8 and perform it over a classmate playing dotted quarter notes on a drum.
study.source: Original activity written for this lesson; "Pop Goes the Weasel" and "Row, Row, Row Your Boat" are traditional songs in the public domain.
steps: Count and step 6/8 with accents on 1 and 4
discussion: How did stepping in 6/8 feel different from 4/4?
Why does 6/8 feel like two beats, not six?
What kinds of music often use compound metre?
study.product: Write a short explanation of simple and compound metre with one rhythm example of each, then compose and label a two-bar 6/8 rhythm.

items.answer: A metre where each beat divides into three.

items.q: How many main beats are in a bar of 6/8?

items.answer: 6/8 has two beats divided in three; 4/4 has four beats divided in two.

items.q: Name two songs or styles in compound metre.
Why is 6/8 felt as two beats?
items.answer: The eighth notes group into two sets of three.

items.q: Compose and label a two-bar 6/8 rhythm.

items.answer: 6/8 is two groups of three; 3/4 is three groups of two.
